Major Policies to be

TOO MANY DELAYS

Responsible Men Desired
in the North

Japan had recognized the Nanking
administration as the Central Govern-
ment of China, and will in the future
continue to deal exclusively with it
in national affairs, Maj.-Gen. Yasuji
Okamura, Chief of the Second De-
partment of the Army General Staff,
told Japanese reporters yesterday
afternoon.
There was a pressing need for the
appointment of officials in north
China, who could negotiate on various
matters without constantly seeking
instructions from Nanking, Maj.-Gen.
Okamura said.
The Japanese officer, who arrived
to convey to the officials stationed
here Tokyo's latest policies towards
China, recalled that much delay at-
tended the enforcement of the Tangku
Peace Agreement, as the Chinese re-
ferred all minor details to Nanking
for confirmation.
Maj.-Gen. Okamura said that he had
not seen any Chinese officials during
his present visit because he thought
it of little use in view of the "current
features of Chinese Government."

Improvement in the North

Commenting on the Dairen and
Shanghai conferences of military
officers stationed in Manchoukuo and
China, he said that it was gratifying
to see the complete accord of views
existing between the Central Army
authorities and military representa-
tives in these two countries.
At the two conferences, he added,
he explained the views of the Tokyo
authorities on the rapidly changing
situation in Europe, concentrating his
attention on the Italo-Ethiopian con-
flict.
Maj.-Gen. Okamura denied the
current rumours that the two
meetings were called to decide Ja-
pan's policy towards China and
Manchoukuo. This policy, he said,
will always be decided in Tokyo and
no local conference of such nature
could be entrusted with deciding
Japan's actions.
He revealed that the Central Army
authorities will convene such meet-
ings frequently in the future.
There has been a marked improve-
ment in the political atmosphere in
north China since his last visit there
at the end of 1934, although there
are constant changes in the adminis-
tration of the region.

日本与

重大政策将在

延误过多

北方需要

日本已承认南京政府为中国的中央政府，今后在国家事务上将继续 exclusively 与其打交道，陆军参谋本部第二部部长冈村 Yasuji 少将昨天下午对日本记者表示。
冈村少将称，华北急需任命官员，这些官员应能就各种事项进行谈判，而无需不断向南京请示。
这位日本军官此行旨在向驻此地的官员传达东京对华最新政策，他回顾说，《塘沽停战协定》的执行因诸多延误而受阻，因为中方将所有细枝末节都提交南京确认。
冈村少将表示，他在此次访问期间未会见任何中国官员，因为他认为鉴于“中国政府目前的状况”，此举并无多大用处。

华北局势改善

在评论驻扎在满洲国和中国的军事官员在大连和上海举行的会议时，他表示，看到中央陆军当局与这两个国家的军事代表之间观点完全一致，令人欣慰。
他补充说，在这两次会议上，他解释了东京当局对欧洲迅速变化的局势的看法，重点关注意埃冲突。
冈村少将否认了目前关于这两次会议旨在决定日本对华及对满洲国政策的谣言。他说，这一政策将始终在东京决定，此类性质的地方会议无权决定日本的行动。
他透露，中央陆军当局将来会经常召开此类会议。
自1934年底上次访问以来，尽管该地区的行政管理层不断变动，但华北的政治氛围已有显著改善。

In connection with the conference of Japanese military
officers which is to take place in the residence of Major-

do not intend to ask for police protection, but that they have
no objection to such protection being afforded by the Japanese
Consular Police or the Shanghai Municipal Police if it is
deemed necessary.

Commissioner, (S.B.), I have to report that the local Japanese
Consular Police are at present considering the precautionary
measures to be adopted at the conference, but up to the
present no definite arrangements have been made. A further
report will be forwarded as soon as arrangements are completed.

The Japanese Military Police have decided to detail one
officer in plain-clothes to meet Major-General Okamura,
Chief of the Second Section of the General Staff, who will
arrive from Nanking by train at the Shanghai North Station
at 7.15 a.m. October 19. Two gendarmerie officers in uniform
and one in plain-clothes will also be detailed for duty
at the residence of Major-General Isogai during the period
of the conference.

The programme of the conference will be drawn up after
the arrival of Major-General Okamura.

At 6.30 p.m. October 19, a dinner party will be held
at the Japanese Club, Boone Road, at which military officers
only will be present.

JAPANESE MILITARY OFFICERS TO HOLD CONFERENCE
IN SHANGHAI

High Japanese officials have been delegated
to China by both the War Office and the Foreign Office
of the Japanese Government to convey the resolutions passed
at a conference which was recently held in Tokyo by the
Foreign Office, the War Office, the Navy Office and the
Finance Office for the purpose of discussing Japan's future
policy towards China. With a view to accelerating these
resolutions, a conference has been held by the Japanese
military officials at Dairen. It is now learnt that a
conference of Japanese military officers will be held in
Shanghai on October 20 when all the Japanese Consuls in
various parts of this country will attend.

A certain spokesman of the local Japanese
Embassy, when interviewed by a reporter of the Sin Sun
News Agency, stated that as a result of the resolutions
adopted by the four Ministries regarding Japan's new policy
towards China, officers had been despatched to China by
the War Office and the Foreign Office to convey these
decisions to both the Japanese military officials and
Consuls in China. The conference which was held at Dairen
was for the purpose of transmitting these resolutions
to the military officers of the Japanese Kwantung Army and
the Japanese Forces in North China. The conference in
Shanghai will be of a similar nature, i.e. to convey these
principles to the Japanese Consuls and Navy officers in
China. He further declared that the conference at Dairen
terminated on the night of October 14. He concluded by
saying that the recent visit to Tientsin of Mr. Matsuoka,
President of the Manchurian Railways was for the purpose
of discussing financial problems with Major-General Okamura.

一支强大的政府军部队正与红军作战。

China Evening News published the following editorial
on October 14.-

JAPAN'S NEW POLICY TOWARDS CHINA

The Ministries of Foreign Affairs,
War, Navy and Finance of Japan have passed a new policy
to deal with China. A meeting of Japanese military
officers has been held in Dairen and another meeting of
a similar nature will be held in Shanghai. We do
not want to make any comment on the new policy because
it has not yet been formally proclaimed.
Japan is now worrying on our behalf
about the situation in our country - an action which
is entirely unnecessary. Our domestic affairs will
be dealt with by our own Government; there is no need for
foreign countries to concern themselves in our home
affairs.
Japan should be held responsible for
the critical situation in North China. The rebellious
elements who have made the demilitarized zone their den
have been the chief source of troubles and disturbances
in Hopei Province.
If Japan is sincere in maintaining
peace in the Far East and in cooperating with China, she
should first restore to us our lost territory and
abolish all war treaties. Japan's military and
diplomatic officers are very active inspite of her
intentions to maintain peace. As a consequence
doubts and misunderstanding arise on all sides.
Japan seems, indeed, to be doing something contrary
to her announcement.

《中国晚报》（China Evening News）于10月14日发表以下社论：

日本对华新政策

日本外务、陆军、海军和财务四省已通过一项处理对华事务的新政策。日本军官已在大连举行会议，另一场类似性质的会议将在上海举行。我们不想对新政策做任何评论，因为它尚未正式公布。
日本现在正替我们担忧我国的局势——这是一种完全不必要的举动。我们的内政将由我们自己的政府处理；外国无需关心我们的内部事务。
日本应对华北的危急局势负责。那些以非军事区为巢穴的反叛分子一直是河北省麻烦和动荡的主要根源。
如果日本真诚希望维持远东和平并与中国合作，她首先应归还我们失地并废除所有不平等条约。尽管日本声称希望维持和平，但其军事和外交官员却非常活跃。因此，各方产生了怀疑和误解。
日本所做的似乎确实与其声明背道而驰。
